title: Extension of a small affine germ cocone to an etale scheme chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, and $\bar x:h_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}\to X$ a geometric point over $S$. Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme, $e:h_T\to X$ a representable etale map, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ an $S$-map with $e\bar t=\bar x$. Write $D_X$ for the opposite-indexed regular-function diagram on small pointed affine $X$-neighbourhoods [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models, def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], and $D_T$ for the regular-function diagram on affine pointed etale $T$-neighbourhoods of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $c$ be any commutative-ring cocone on $D_X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. There exists a natural transformation $\gamma:D_T\to\operatorname{const}(c.\mathrm{pt})$ satisfying the following two assertions. Every affine pointed $T$-neighbourhood $(N,\bar n)$ admits a small pointed affine $X$-neighbourhood $(M,\bar m)$ and an $S$-map $a:M\to N$ whose composite to $X$ equals the chart map of $M$ and with $a\bar m=\bar n$. For every such $N,M,a$, one has $\gamma_N=c_M\circ\Gamma(a)$. Neither a universal property for $c$ nor one for $\gamma$ is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Compose N -> T with e. Scheme-test etaleness and its composition law in def-trf-algebraic-space make this an affine etale X-chart. The small skeleton equivalence in def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model transports this affine chart and its geometric pointing to a small pointed neighbourhood M, giving the specified morphism a. In fact an isomorphic representative can be used, so this gives the refinement assertion even without a surjectivity assumption on e.

proof.text: For each affine pointed T-neighbourhood N, choose such M and a and set γ_N=Γ(a) followed by c_M. Any two choices have a common pointed affine refinement over N; replace this by its small skeleton representative. The two cocone identities for c identify the two composites. For a pointed transition Nprime -> N, perform the same comparison over Nprime to obtain naturality of γ. Comparing with any given compatible M and a proves the stipulated formula. The refinement and comparison concern the actual regular-function diagrams, so no algebra structure or arbitrary existence witness is substituted for their data.

theorem schemeChart_germCocone
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk s) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (T : Over S)
    (e : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.obj.obj) (he : IsEtale e)
    (t : Over.mk s ⟶ T) (ht : yoneda.map t ≫ e = x)
    (c : Cocone (ringDiagram x)) :
    ∃ γ : Scheme.strictHenselizationDiagram t.left ⟶
        (Functor.const _).obj c.pt,
      (∀ N : Scheme.AffinePointedEtaleNeighborhood t.left,
        ∃ (M : Neighbourhood (Over.mk s) x)
          (a : ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.left ⟶
            Over.mk (N.obj.1.hom ≫ T.hom)),
          (yoneda.map (a ≫ Over.homMk N.obj.1.hom) ≫ e =
            ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.hom) ∧
          M.hom.left.left ≫ a.left = N.obj.2.left) ∧
      (∀ (N : Scheme.AffinePointedEtaleNeighborhood t.left)
        (M : Neighbourhood (Over.mk s) x)
        (a : ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.left ⟶
          Over.mk (N.obj.1.hom ≫ T.hom)),
        yoneda.map (a ≫ Over.homMk N.obj.1.hom) ≫ e =
            ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.hom →
        M.hom.left.left ≫ a.left = N.obj.2.left →
        γ.app (op N) = a.left.appTop ≫ c.ι.app (op M))
